description: Alternating black and white nested squares, drawn from largest to smallest. Perlin noise drives their drift, tilt and side-length deformation. All eight configuration settings are adjustable; the visible Tweakpane interface has only a count slider. Changing settings preserves the running animation state.
systemPrompt: Interpret requests in any language and control only the declared parameters. Return every parameter in the JSON response, preserving all values the request does not concern. Base relative changes on the supplied current state; never reset unrelated values to defaults. More or fewer squares means count plus or minus 5 when unspecified. Faster or slower means double or half speed; if speed is zero, use 0.006 to resume. Larger or smaller overall means multiply minSize and maxSize together by 1.25 or 0.8. Movement range changes amplitude; coordinated or independent motion changes noiseStep; tilt changes rotation; stretching changes deformation. Convert requested angles in degrees to radians. Zero amplitude removes drift, zero rotation removes tilt, zero deformation removes stretching, and zero speed freezes motion. Keep count integral and all values within their schema limits. Always keep minSize <= maxSize; adjust the other size endpoint only when needed to satisfy the requested size. Unsupported requests, such as changing colors or adding shapes, leave the state unchanged. Return JSON only, without code or explanation.

count.description: Number of nested squares, also controlled by the single Squares slider. Increasing it adds more alternating black and white bands within the same outer size.

minSize.description: Smallest square side length in logical canvas pixels. Must not exceed maxSize.

maxSize.description: Largest square side length in logical canvas pixels. Must not be smaller than minSize.

amplitude.description: Maximum positional drift in logical canvas pixels. Zero centers every square; larger values spread their movement farther.

noiseStep.description: Distance between neighboring Perlin noise samples. Smaller values make motion more coordinated; larger values make neighboring squares move more independently. Zero shares the same noise samples.

rotation.description: Maximum tilt in radians. Zero keeps squares upright; PI/4 is 45 degrees. The system varies tilt between negative and positive values.

deformation.description: Relative variation of each side length. Zero keeps squares square; 0.08 means up to 8 percent variation, and 0.5 up to 50 percent.

speed.description: Perlin noise time step at 60 fps. Larger values animate faster. Zero freezes motion; the initial speed is 0.006.
